item.description:
Lets get this bread
It's fucking exhausting.
Hard to hunt mammoth when you killed them all, boomer.
Having a day where I don't want to get out of bed again. Gloomy mood today. Finished a poem last night, based on the Wagtail Chase. Attached it at the end of the post.
We are big on anti-clanker roleplay.
Oops needed to save this for a future Bronze-age history dump. Just like I needed to save the LOTR memes for a LOTR dump... Eh, what does it matter, the world is burning and people are dying because rich people need more yacht money.
Also pissed that I'm being cited for holding a cellphone when it was Pippin's fucking food dish when The Pippin came with me to Prescott yesterday. Debating whether to fight it [because you fucking know his camera was off] or just lay back and take the $280 fine up my ass.
Third option for Hard-boiled Hadrosaur Detective.
It's Parasaurolophus
Nyctosaurus man, what a batshit pterosaur
Pippin tax Today's message from Pippin: "fuck you" [kissing noises] ___ 1) Are you on the run to a safe place and passing through Arizona on your way to safer grounds? My apartment is open to you to crash at, and it is a safe space. Pippin and I will make you a meal and gladly share tea, wine, or mead with you. 2) Hey! Take your meds with a full glass of water, please. Do it for Pippin, or Space Mom, or better yet, do it for yourself. 3) Ĝefeloað wē. We will carry on. 4) all funds from the sales of items at these two links will be sent to support charities aiding to fight for Trans rights in the US (not just T-shirts!) https://www.teepublic.com/t-shirt/74812801-all-conures-are-anarchists https://www.teepublic.com/t-shirt/74811778-whiptail-pride 5) Since multiple people have requested this over the last two weeks or so, my ko-fi is: https://ko-fi.com/codyandpippin
New poem [as yet untitled]: I race towards the metaphor, Wheels throbbing on pavement at 80 Hurtling like a brilliant Bollide across lost seas and ancient lava fields Oj Lazare echoing in my ears Hurrying north through the dawn light Advancing forth in search of destiny: A tiny lost white bird who found himself becoming an allegorical poetry subject. Life is funny like that: Somehow, the national bird of Latvia, Is reportedly hanging around a pond In the Arizona high country. We are always more lost than we think, But we are never As broken as we think we are; Or so I hope. Maybe. I don't know why I search for good omens In a world literally on fire Filled with blood Running like rivers. It will all end the same anyway: Badly. Why bother? There are no good omens In this world anymore. The world is gone mad, And there is nothing to look forward to anymore. The rich have bought our future Leaving us with nothing. The bird is lost because the world Is wrong in every way. I have nothing to look forward to. I know you will ghost me The first chance you get: I've never been anyone's First choice. And I never will be; I am sacred enough for friendship, But not holy enough to be loved. It is what it is; How else could it be otherwise? And, like clockwork, The Wagtail never shows; And nobody simply Will let me die.

item.title: GovBrief Today #550
item.description: Border agents swabbed a four-year-old's cheek and uploaded her DNA to the FBI's criminal database. Federal agents sent more than 2,700 records into that database every day last year, nearly a million in all, most from people never charged with any crime. Immigration enforcement now captures more profiles than any police force in the country, and the process could not be easier. All it takes is a cotton swab. No judge signs off, and agents swab nearly everyone they detain. Participation is required. A man who arrived for a probation appointment in Waco found ICE waiting, was ordered to open his mouth, prosecuted when he refused, and convicted. Genetic data sits in federal computers with no expiration date, and DNA never describes just one person. The four-year-old's file can be used to identify her parents, her siblings, and relatives she will never meet. I've emailed 8,501 stories over 550 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. item.title: Happy "There Will Come Soft Rains" Day
item.description:
The original short story, written by Ray Bradbury in 1950 is set today, August 4th 2026. It's brief and brilliant, and if you've not read it, or haven't read it in a while, here's a copy: https://www.btboces.org/Downloads/7_There%20Will%20Come%20Soft%20Rains%20by%20Ray%20Bradbury.pdf
In 1952, Weird Fantasy, the EC Comics anthology series, published an adaptation by the amazing Wally Wood.
The original story is better than the comic, imo, if only for the creeping sense of dread. The part about the dog, left out of the comic is a little heartbreaking.
The story was collected, along with a ton of Bradbury's other sci-fi shorts, into a "Fix Up Novel," which is what you call it when disparate short stories are made into a single book, called The Martian Chronicles.
The Martian Chronicles was adapted into a TV Miniseries starring an HIV positive Rock Hudson in one of his final roles. There Will Come Soft Rains was left out of the adaptation.
Apparently there was a radio adaptation in the early 1950s, and luminaries from Leonard Nimoy to Burgess Meredith have recorded adaptions
But my favorite version remains the original. Happy There Will Come Soft Rains Day to you all.
